items.summary: Singapore Airlines (SIA) reported on Nov 16 that passenger traffic rose 3. 5% in October from the year-ago period, driven by resilient air travel demand. SIA together with its budget arm Scoot carried 3. 7 million passengers during the month, up 4. 5% from a year earlier, per a bourse filing. The group's October passenger capacity rose 2. 9%, while the passenger load factor (PLF) climbed 0. 5 percentage point to 87. 8%. SIA recorded a monthly PLF of 86. 8%, supported by robust growth across all regions including East Asia, Europe and the South-west Pacific, where traffic marginally trailed capacity increases.
items.title: Singapore Airlines Reports October Traffic and Cargo Results

items.summary:
US President Donald Trump said he "would certainly not mind" seeing former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang reinstated as his job, expressing a view that allies of the ousted boss have backed through an open letter demanding his return. Huang resigned last week after two affairs emerged: one with Alice Huang, suspected of spying for China and denied by Beijing, and another allegedly with an Nvidia executive who reported to him directly. The resignations created a crisis at one of the world's most valuable firms and a key AI industry player.

Fellow tech bosses including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Epic Games' Tim Sweeney joined more than 175,000 signatories in backing a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign urging Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang while an internal probe continued. The Stand with Jensen group claimed the removal lacked meaningful due process, though BBC reporting suggested his reinstatement was unlikely while investigations ran.
items.title: Trump Says He Wouldn't Mind Seeing Jensen Huang Return to Nvidia

items.summary:
The article opens with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid a wave of scandals, noting that questions persist about the Trump administration's handling of the situation—specifically whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick shielded Nvidia. Despite his misdeeds, Huang retains Silicon Valley supporters including Elon Musk and others who dispute that his errors warranted removal; President Donald Trump had urged him to fight for his job. A central concern is how the fallout affects US-China relations, particularly chip and AI policy ahead of talks in Shenzhen, where Georgetown's Mark MacCarthy sees tighter export controls likely but an intact AI safety dialogue. Huang's downfall may also reignite debate over banning Chinese open-weight models, even though Nvidia had defended them against a reported Washington push to prohibit them.

On settlements and accountability, states will receive at least $1. 2 billion a year from Meta over ten years (up to $16.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Resignation and Global Tech Policy Developments

items.summary:
Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang is weighing a return to the company after resigning amid reports that he had affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate. The resignation has triggered a spectacular leadership crisis at the $4 trillion chipmaker, prompting an independent board probe into the conduct in question. Despite his departure, several confidants say Huang has discussed returning with close allies even as Nvidia's board investigates.

A group of Silicon Valley executives is reportedly assembling what one ally described to the FT as a 'war room' to lobby for the former chief's reinstatement and would seek support from the White House.
items.title: Jensen Huang allies build a 'war room' to get him back at Nvidia

items.summary: On Monday, Google announced new features for its Maps service built around generative AI that help users plan trips and handle everyday tasks. The company is introducing the ability to create step-by-step trip itineraries through an “Ask Maps” tool, which lets people pull up directions and receive real-time details about their route right away. Users can build plans ranging from a holiday shopping day trip to more complex arrangements such as a three-day road trip featuring coastal hikes and oceanfront dining.
items.title: Google Maps Adds AI-Powered Trip Itineraries and Agentic Appointments

items.summary: The article argues that Nvidia was already facing competitive pressures before the ousting of CEO Jensen Huang, who is credited with foreseeing AI trends and investing early in training chips. Now under CFO Colette Kress, the company must plan two years ahead for an industry shifting fast. Nvidia still dominates AI accelerators at 80 percent of sales (Silicon Analysis), but rivals are closing in: AMD's share rose from 2 percent in 2022 to between 7 and 10 percent by 2026, while US cloud players Google, Amazon and Microsoft build their own specialized silicon to cut costs and reduce dependence on Nvidia. Startups such as Cerebras sell large chips for big models; AMD acquired Taalas to burn model weights into silicon; and Nvidia bought the chip startup Groq in December 2025.
items.title: Nvidia's Dominance Under Threat as Competitors and China Rise

items.summary: Microsoft has again reminded customers that Windows Server 2016 will stop receiving security updates upon reaching end of support in roughly two months. This follows an October warning announcing the end of extended support for Windows Server 2016 and encouraging users to upgrade to Windows Server 2025. The product reached general availability on October 12, 2016, one month after its official release at Microsoft's annual Ignite conference in September of that year. It also reached the end of mainstream support nearly 4 years ago, in January 2022, and extended support will end in roughly two months, on January 13, 2027.
items.title: Microsoft Windows Server 2016 End of Support and Upgrade Guidance

items.summary:
Google is launching new features in its Ask Maps tool to help users manage holiday travel and preparation more easily. The updates let people build step-by-step trip itineraries with real-time route details, including live traffic conditions, whether a place is open, and the general vibe at upcoming stops. Users can create day trips for shopping or longer multi-day road trips with numbered map pins and insider tips for each stop, then share the itinerary with friends and family or export it to Google Docs on desktop.

For holiday prep, Ask Maps gains agentic capabilities that let users ask questions like "Find me a 4 p.
items.title: New Google Maps 'Ask Maps' Features for Holiday Travel and Prep

items.summary:
Public discourse on Singapore's ageing population largely centres on chronic illnesses, healthcare costs and long-term care. Yet one equally real aspect of ageing remains largely taboo: the sexual needs of seniors. The article illustrates this through the case of a relatively healthy 65-year-old man who still experiences normal sexual desires while his spouse has lost interest in intimacy; unwilling to betray a decades-long marriage yet reluctant to accept lifelong repression simply due to age, he faces a quiet dilemma that an ageing society must confront.

Seniors' sexual needs are not merely private matters. They intersect with medical health, marital dynamics and social safety.
items.title: Addressing Seniors' Sexual Health Is Key to Their Ageing with Dignity and Safety

items.summary: Three cyclists died in Singapore between 11 and 13 November — a 37-year-old woman in Katong, a 24-year-old man in Changi, and a 75-year-old man in Hougang; two were struck by tipper trucks. In response, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) published guidance on how cyclists should ride near buses, advice that columnist Preeti Mohan supports as a cyclist but argues runs only one direction of road safety.
items.title: Enforce Rules on Errant Cyclists, But Road Safety Runs Both Ways

items.summary:
The Trump administration is preparing interim export controls on advanced artificial intelligence chips and servers that would extend U. S. restrictions beyond direct sales, targeting remote access to computing power located outside the United States. Under the rule from the Commerce Department, companies must obtain licenses to export, reexport or transfer AI chips and servers to data centers anywhere in the world if those facilities may provide compute to firms in China or other restricted countries.

The controls apply to entities based in a group of embargoed nations that includes China, Russia, Iran, North Korea and 18 others.
items.title: US Tightens AI Chip Export Controls to Block Remote Access for Chinese Firms

items.summary: Arion Kurtaj, a 21-year-old hacker from Oxford, pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to breaching Rockstar Games and several other companies. He had originally been deemed unfit for trial due to the severity of his autism and was sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital; however, doctors later assessed him as fit to stand trial, leading to his release into a normal prison in January. Kurtaj carried out the hack on Rockstar Games in 2022 while he was on bail for other hacking offences and under police protection, being housed in a Travelodge in Bicester to shield him from rival hackers who threatened him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. Using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel room television along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, Kurtaj stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished Grand Theft Auto 6.
items.title: GTA 6 Hacker Arion Kurtaj Pleads Guilty After Release From Secure Hospital

items.summary: On the early morning of May 31, 2026, on southbound Interstate 75 near Naples, Florida, an overturned box truck blocked lanes and was struck by a Tesla Model 3 traveling at high speed. The crash killed two teenage passengers in the car plus Jonathan Garcia Arias, a 25-year-old former Marine who had stopped to help; the driver and two other occupants were seriously injured. Local police and media reported it as an ordinary truck wreck in the dark, with no mention of any driver-assist system. Tesla's own report filed under NHTSA's Standing General Order contradicts that framing: its telematics show Autopilot or Full Self-Driving was 'Verified Engaged,' a pre-crash speed of 71 mph is logged, and a fatality is recorded. At the same time, Tesla redacted the crash narrative, software version, and whether the road fell within the system's approved operating domain as confidential business information — the same treatment applied to roughly 99.
items.title: Tesla on Autopilot/FSD hit an overturned truck at 71 mph, killing 3

items.summary: French PV manufacturer HoloSolis has completed a Series A funding round of more than €15 million ($16. 5 million), bringing on four new shareholders: French banking group Crédit Agricole through four regional banks, investment management firm Algebris, Chinese solar module manufacturer Trina Solar, and Chinese EV charging and energy storage specialist StarCharge. The new investors join existing backers including EIT InnoEnergy, IDEC Group, independent power producer TSE, and Calès Technologies.
items.title: HoloSolis Secures €15 Million Series A to Build 5 GW Solar Factory in France

items.summary:
A petition calling for Jensen Huang to be reinstated as Nvidia CEO has drawn more than 178,000 signatures in the four days following his resignation after revelations of extramarital affairs. The "Stand With Jensen" campaign listed prominent Silicon Valley figures among its signatories, including Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney. Of those identified their affiliations, more than 8,400 said they were current Nvidia employees and nearly 90,000 described themselves as shareholders, though the campaign cautioned that these professional ties were self-reported and had not been independently verified.

The turmoil comes as Nvidia takes on growing strategic importance in Washington.
items.title: Silicon Valley Leaders Back Call for Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia

items.summary: Following co-founder Jensen Huang's sudden resignation after disclosures of extramarital affairs, including a relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang—whom U. S. authorities suspect may be linked to Chinese intelligence agencies—the AI industry is grappling with questions about Nvidia's leadership and future. IBM Chairman and CEO Arvind Krishna addressed the impact, telling Moneycontrol that within the next 2 to 3 years, no major effect on AI-industry investment is expected. He noted Nvidia already has sufficient orders and commitments to keep its engineers busy for two more years, giving the company time to select a new CEO and manage leadership transitions.
items.title: Jensen Huang के बिना कैसे चलेगी Nvidia? IBM CEO ने अगले 3 साल को लेकर दिया बड़ा बयान

items.summary: Following the sudden departure of CEO Jensen Huang amid revelations of extramarital affairs—including one involving a suspected Chinese spy—attention has shifted from Nvidia's narrowing margins to more fundamental questions about its influence across the AI ecosystem. Finance chief Colette Kress now serves as interim CEO while the board selects an external search firm for a permanent successor. The company is set to report third-quarter earnings after market close on Tuesday, with analysts expecting results similar to prior quarters but focused heavily on management changes and interim strategy.
items.title: Nvidia's Post-Huang Leadership Crisis and Earnings Outlook

items.summary:
This news roundup presents five major stories from India covering fuel prices, budget tax expectations, Air India route changes and the return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The central question driving the fuel-price story is why petrol and diesel prices have not fallen even as crude oil becomes cheaper; Central Petroleum Minister Suresh Gopi explained that oil companies are facing significant economic pressure, leaving consumers without visible relief despite ongoing price-cut expectations.

On fiscal matters, investors' hopes for long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax relief ahead of the 2027 budget have grown.
items.title: Top 5 Stories: पेट्रोल-डीजल की कीमतों में राहत कब, Air India की फ्लाइट्स में बदलाव और Nvidia में Jensen Huang की वापसी की हलचल समेत पढ़ें 5 बड़ी खबरें

items.summary: Pressure from the US government on Nvidia has intensified over whether the chipmaker knowingly permitted the sale of restricted technology to China, as a separate scandal widened around ousted CEO Jensen Huang and his affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. The ex-Nvidia chief has agreed to testify behind closed doors before US lawmakers, while Treasury secretary Jack Lew questioned whether the firm pursued sales to China in order to boost revenues and demanded a “dramatic shakeup” at the company as reports circulated of Huang seeking a path back to his job.
items.title: Government Pressure Mounts on Nvidia Over China Technology-Sale Spying Scandal

items.summary:
International remittances help households meet daily needs and insure against hardship, yet the average fee for an ordinary transfer still stands at around 6%, far above the UN Sustainable Development Goals target of below 3% by 2030. New research by Flori and Limodio (2026) argues that a missing piece in explaining these high costs is the exchange rate risk borne by money transfer operators, or MTOs.

The exposure arises because an intermediary quotes an exchange rate and commits to delivering a fixed amount of foreign currency, but must later buy it at whatever price prevails. If the recipient's currency strengthens before settlement, the operator loses; in thin, underdeveloped FX markets—where depth rises steeply with GDP per capita—this risk cannot be hedged cheaply and so enters the marginal cost of every transfer. Competition alone therefore cannot remove it: competition squeezes markups but a corridor can still be highly competitive and very expensive.

Using the World Bank's Remittance Prices Worldwide database on 34,680 transfers across 339 corridors between 2011 and 2024, they find that fees rise with currency volatility rather than GDP. During episodes of exceptional instability, costs rose by about $1 on a US$200 transfer; in the quarter of the Swiss National Bank's unexpected abandonment of the franc's floor against the euro on 15 January 2015, prices jumped almost $1.60 relative to unexposed corridors—about 11% of the average cost ($14). The effect was stronger for thinner currency markets and less geographically diversified operators.

Estimating a model of the remittance market against a counterfactual with fixed exchange rates, they conclude that currency risk contributes about as much to fees as markups on average. Its share is highest in South America (24%) and sub-Saharan Africa (22%). The authors note this hits migrants twice—through higher prices now and reduced competition over time—and argue policy should promote deeper FX markets, affordable hedging instruments, and liquidity during market stress.

The study's boundaries include its reliance on the 2015 Swiss franc shock as a causal instrument for an event unrelated to migrant behaviour, and regional shares reported only as averages. Sources draw on BIS Triennial Survey data, World Bank indicators, Bloomberg, and Flori and Limodio (2026).
items.title: Currency Risk Drives Remittance Fees as Much as Markups Do

items.summary:
This post compares subjective beliefs about future job-finding and job-loss prospects from the New York Fed's Survey of Consumer Expectations (SCE) with their realized counterparts in the Current Population Survey (CPS). Before COVID, aggregate expectations aligned closely with actual rates: averaged over 2014 through 2019, the SCE expected a three-month job-finding rate of 55. 5 percent versus a CPS true rate of 57. 2 percent. The steep drop in realized three-month-ahead job finding at the end of 2019 reflected the unanticipated arrival of COVID-19; expectations fell only at its onset in March 2020, and although actual rates largely recovered to pre-COVID levels by 2021, expectations remained subdued. In the years after 2020, realized job-finding rates averaged 58. 8 percent from 2022 onward while predicted probabilities fell to 53. 0 percent, indicating persistent post-pandemic pessimism about finding a job.

This divergence was driven primarily by younger individuals and those without college education.
items.title: Can Workers Predict Job Finding and Job Loss?

items.summary:
This FRED Blog post revisits the many ways of measuring unemployment, noting that there are six official definitions—U-1 through U-6—with some constants and several variations, including notable regional differences. The authors describe each measure as a separate map built from FRED data, where darker shading indicates higher rates under most maps.

The first definition, U-1 (Unemployed 15 weeks and over), focuses on the long-term unemployed—persons likely having the most in trouble in the labor market—and shows lower rates in the Mountain region, about-average rates in the South, and higher rates elsewhere.
items.title: Geographic differences in unemployment definitions: a regional walk through FRED's U-1 to U-6 measures

items.summary: Young adults in advanced economies have grown more pessimistic about their economic prospects in recent years, while gambling-like financial activities have proliferated. Costas Arkolakis, Spencer Y. Kwon, Dominic Russel, Claire Shi, and Hyunjoo Yang link these trends through a Friedman-Savage (1948) motive: when life goals such as homeownership or marriage seem out of reach, individuals turn to financial gambles. The authors test this theory using an original survey combined with millions of linked records from Korea's leading credit bureau, telecom provider, and credit card issuer.
items.title: Gambling for Goals -- by Costas Arkolakis, Spencer Y. Kwon, Dominic Russel, Claire Shi, Hyunjoo Yang

items.summary: In the NBER Working Paper 36011, Jitendra Aswani and Roberto Rigobon examine how sustainable investment affects corporate governance adoption. Using data on 3,944 sustainable bond issuances by public firms from 2013 to 2022, they apply a heteroskedasticity-based identification strategy that finds a 1% increase in sustainable debt (measured relative to total debt) raises the likelihood of adopting sustainable governance practices by 9. 2%. This adoption is associated with an improvement in environmental performance of 16%, according to structural estimates.
items.title: Sustainable Bonds and Governance Adoption: A Causal Analysis of Public Firms (2013–2022)

items.summary: Jim Ratcliffe's Ineos Group has reached an out-of-court settlement with Sir Ben Ainslie over the £180m yacht their companies built for the 2024 America's Cup, and Ineos states it considers the matter closed. The two had worked closely during two cycles of the event, culminating in Ineos Britannia becoming the first British crew to win the challenger series in Barcelona in 2024 — a boat beaten 7-2 by Emirates Team New Zealand that year. They later fell out over plans for a third bid; Ineos announced last year it had
items.title: Ineos Settles America's Cup Yacht Dispute with Ainslie

items.summary:
The European Central Bank has warned that investors could suffer heavy losses if confidence in artificial intelligence falters, cautioning that a reassessment of the AI narrative may trigger an abrupt repricing in markets and significant valuation losses. ECB vice-president Boris Vujčić made the warning while speaking in Frankfurt on Monday, noting that the rapid expansion of AI is creating new challenges for financial stability across the 21-country eurozone. He observed that historically such surges have often coincided with market peaks, pointing to the risk of excessive investor optimism.

The ECB noted that major US tech companies are projected to spend a combined $5.
items.title: ECB Warns AI Share Boom Could End in Abrupt Repricing

items.summary: President Trump said he “wouldn’t mind” seeing Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO, following Huang's resignation last week amid reports of extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy. Speaking to reporters on Monday, Trump added that Huang had “learned a big lesson. ” The remarks came as tech executives—including Elon Musk—have called for Huang's reinstatement in an online petition calling on Nvidia, which has gained more than 160,000 signatures.
items.title: Trump Says He 'Wouldn't Mind' Jensen Huang Being Reinstated as Nvidia CEO

items.summary: Charli D’Amelio rose to TikTok fame at 15 with a single viral dance video, becoming the platform’s first creator to reach 50 million followers in 2019 and later surpassing 100 million. By age 16 she left high school for homeschooling, then abandoned studies entirely as social media became her full-time job and source of income not only for herself but her entire family. She built a brand empire through collaborations—including with Jennifer Lopez—and the family launched The D’Amelio Show on Disney+, which premiered September 3, 2021, and ran two seasons until 2025. Behind the spectacle, she faced mounting pressure: by age 17 she carried responsibilities beyond most teens, and fame exacted a toll on her mental health as she felt responsible for supporting her family through ventures including Be Happy Snacks popcorn.
items.title: Charli D’Amelio’s Break from Family and Fame

items.summary: The Guardian has revealed that the Israeli military uploaded 3. 5m photos to Amazon's cloud platform, Rekognition, using its AI-powered image analysis technology to examine images of Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank (s0). The large catalogue was moved into an Amazon datacentre near Tel Aviv by a department within a military software unit commonly known as Rolling Stone, which holds extensive databases on Palestinian populations including personal details, property holdings, checkpoint crossings, work permits and criminal records (s2-s7). According to leaked documents obtained for the investigation, Israel informed Amazon of its decision in early 2024 so it could use Rekognition for a facial recognition project (s3). The images were uploaded during the early months of Israel's aerial bombardment and ground offensive in Gaza following the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when soldiers routinely collected images at checkpoints that functioned as pop-up surveillance posts (s1-s9). It remains unclear whether these 3.
items.title: Israel Uploaded Millions of Photos to Amazon's Facial Recognition Platform Amid Gaza War

items.summary: US President Donald Trump said Monday that he may raise the issue of Chinese espionage allegations involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during his upcoming meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Speaking to reporters while departing the White House for his Asia trip, Trump pushed back against US intelligence assessments concerning Huang's relationship with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, stating, 'I don't know that she is a spy,' and adding, 'Nobody's proven that.' Jensen Huang resigned on Nov.
items.title: Trump Says He 'May' Raise Nvidia Espionage Allegations With Xi Jinping

items.summary:
U. S. Sen. Maria Cantwell demanded immediate action from the Trump administration to block Chinese-linked firms from accessing advanced U. S. artificial intelligence semiconductors, writing a formal letter on Sunday to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Invoking the Export Control Reform Act of 2018, Cantwell faulted Lutnick for leaving overseas data center loopholes open, citing reports that Chinese tech giants Alibaba and ByteDance trained advanced AI models using restricted Nvidia chips despite warnings from the Bureau of Industry and Security, the agency overseeing export controls.

Cantwell noted that U. S.

Raising conflict-of-interest concerns, Cantwell questioned whether a reported $1.
items.title: US senator demands 'immediate action' to close China AI chip loopholes amid Nvidia diversion claims

items.summary: Two young women—Minji of South Korea and Cherry of China—are drawn together by semiconductors that are smaller than a fingernail and found inside phones, cars and tablets. Minji came to China to further her studies after being attracted by Shenzhen's booming tech industry, where she joined the semiconductor sector. Travelling in the opposite direction, Cherry settled in South Korea, where she works as a Chinese-Korean business interpreter with hopes of serving as a bridge for bilateral communication between the two countries. The pair met at an industry exhibition: Minji represented a supplier while Cherry provided on-site language support.
items.title: Small chips connecting young people from China and South Korea

items.summary: In a CGTN First Voice column offering a Chinese perspective on the latest global events, the author argues that the pursuit of a broader trade agreement should be viewed through a larger strategic lens. Reflecting on the past 20 years, over which the path from the vision of a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP) to its realization has been far from smooth, the writer asks why such an arrangement is still needed today and how it might shape the region's future.
items.title: One more trade deal? Think bigger

items.summary:
As Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) prepares to host its 33rd Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province from November 18-19, 2026, the gathering arrives amid heightened geopolitical tensions, rising global tariffs, and economic uncertainty. The meeting's theme—"Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together"—underscores a central message: shared prosperity is best achieved through openness, dialogue, and cooperation rather than restriction.

The article frames China's approach as one of responsible engagement on the global stage, contrasting it with what it describes as reckless moves by other nations aimed at scoring domestic political points. A key illustration of this cooperative model is the China-Chile relationship. Chile, described as China's "oldest friend in South America," has enjoyed strong trade ties for over 50 years; nearly 40% of Chilean exports went to China and around 24% of its imports came from China in 2024—both higher shares than with any other trading partner.
items.title: APEC China 2026: A Pivotal Meeting for Cooperation

items.summary: The article opens with a standard website notice informing readers that browsing implies agreement to the site's use of cookies under its revised Privacy Policy and Terms of Use, noting that cookie settings can be adjusted through the browser. It then pivots to an upcoming event: world leaders are set to gather in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting.
items.title: Shenzhen in One Word: What Visitors Say

items.summary:
The Trump justice department warned Senator Elizabeth Warren of potential significant legal consequences if she fails to preserve records related to investigations into President Donald Trump, marking the latest warning sent by the DOJ to congressional Democrats about their plans to investigate the administration or its associates. In a letter from US attorney Aaron Reitz in Houston, Warren was described as eager to weaponize congressional investigations against Trump's private associates.

Meanwhile, air travel disruptions continued for a third day with more than 10,000 flights affected on Sunday following an extraordinary no-takeoff order blamed by the administration on faulty communications equipment. Transportation secretary Sean Duffy predicted a return to normal by Monday after more than 250 US-related flights were cancelled and there were delays to over 700 scheduled for Monday.

Trump shifted responsibility to the Biden administration, claiming old equipment needed replacement funding. Congress had passed a $12.5bn air traffic control package in 2025 as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, with top House Democrats noting that $8bn remains unobligated and $11bn is unspent.

Trump also scolded a reporter for questioning his focus on White House renovation projects rather than FAA upgrades. Separately, Trump said he would not mind seeing Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO amid an open letter with more than 165,000 signatories demanding his return after resigning over alleged extramarital affairs.

Trump is preparing to depart for Asia on Monday, beginning in Washington before traveling to Manila and Shenzhen. He will attend the Asean summit, meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin for their first trilateral summit, and participate in the Quad partnership meeting with India's Narendra Modi and Australia's Anthony Albanese.

In Alaska's US Senate race between Democrat Mary Peltola and Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan, 97% of ballots had been counted with Peltola at 49.9%, needing more than 50% to win as the state uses ranked-choice run-off elections.
items.title: Trump administration tensions with Democrats amid US air travel chaos and Asia trip

items.summary: Russia says it has recorded its largest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, in which a landmark bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea sustained minor damage and several oil refineries were hit. The Russian military intercepted and destroyed 2,049 drones over 24 hours, officials said, with around 600 flying toward Moscow alone, according to Mayor Sergey Sobyanin. Kyiv came under a record 17 air raid alerts in a single day. At least seven people were killed by Russian strikes, and attacks on energy infrastructure caused blackouts for 50,000 people.
items.title: Russia Reports Biggest Ukrainian Drone Attack of War as Crimea Bridge Sustains Minor Damage

items.summary: At the China (Hainan) Museum of the South China Sea, a wall of photographs pays tribute to generations of fishermen and captains. Among those honored are men who spent their lives navigating distant waters, passing on their knowledge and shaping the fishing culture of the South China Sea.
items.title: The Captains Who Shaped a Fishing Tradition

items.summary: The Recording Academy announced the nominees for its inaugural Best Asian Pop Music Performance category at the upcoming 69th Annual Grammy Awards, to be held in Los Angeles on February 7, 2027. Japan is represented by two acts: metal-meets-idol trio Babymetal and prolific anime singer Lisa (LiSA). They join a pair of South Korean groups—IVE and KIIIKIII—and a pair of rising Philippine pop groups—SB19 and Bini—as the category's nominees, with winners to be revealed at the ceremony.
items.title: Japan’s Babymetal and Lisa Nominated for Inaugural Best Asian Pop Music Performance Grammy Category

items.summary:
A new 2025 census counts just 382 North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis), a decline of about 1. 8% from the 389 animals recorded in 2024, according to scientists at the New England Aquarium's Anderson Cabot Center for Ocean Life and NOAA. The population remains critically endangered by IUCN standards, with only around 73 females of reproductive age holding steady despite the overall drop. A small ray of hope emerged from a record calving season in 2025: 24 new calves were born — the most since 2009 — along with three new mothers. Marine mammal scientist Heather Pettis, who chairs this year's meeting and leads the right whale research program at the Anderson Cabot Center, said seeing the decline is disappointing and that the population is not yet on a clear path to recovery.

The declines come amid regulatory setbacks in the U. S.

In May, Canadian officials expressed concerns about how these U. S.
items.title: North Atlantic Right Whales Hit Record Low Amid Regulatory Rollbacks

items.summary: The official 007 Instagram account has announced that British actor Robert Pattinson will become the next James Bond, making him the first to take on the role since Daniel Craig departed after his 2021 film No Time to Die. Pattinson's film credits this year include The Odyssey and Primetime. He succeeds Craig in a franchise about a secret agent known for his charm, tailored tuxedos, and a fondness for martinis 'shaken, not stirred.' Debuting in 1962, the Bond movies have brought in more than $7 billion in global ticket sales since Sean Connery first brought Agent 007 to the big screen.
items.title: Robert Pattinson Named as the Next James Bond

items.summary: The 2027 Grammy Awards nominations have been announced from New York's Times Square, with British singer Raye leading the field. Raye tops the nominee list with 11 nods, including song of the year and record of the year for 'Where Is My Husband' and album of the year for 'This Music May Contain Hope.' Spanish musician Rosalía followed with nine nominations, coming days after dominating the Latin Grammys with her album Lux. Among Australian artists recognised were Tame Impala, nominated for Record of the Year for Dracula (a collaboration with Jennie), and Baz Luhrmann for Epic: Elvis Presley in Concert. Country music legend Dolly Parton received three posthumous nominations following her death in August. The ceremony is scheduled to take place on Sunday, February 7th - the morning of Monday 8th in Australia time - at Los Angeles.
items.title: 2027 Grammy Award Nominations: Raye Leads as Australian and Spanish Artists Are Recognised

items.summary: CGTN reports that Brazil grows and exports more coffee than any other country in the world. This week, the nation put that position on display during its International Coffee Week event held in the capital of Minas Gerais, a southeastern state responsible for growing roughly half of the country's coffee production. Among the buyers attending were importers from China, underscoring Brazil's role as a leading global supplier of coffee beans to international markets.
items.title: Brazil's International Coffee Week Expected to Generate $35 Million

items.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed support for Jensen Huang being reinstated as Nvidia CEO, telling reporters before departing for his Asia visit that he would not mind the former chief executive returning to the role. Trump framed the situation by suggesting that Huang had learned a significant lesson from his departure, noting that one important lesson outweighs others. When pressed on Alice Huang, the woman with whom Jensen was involved in an affair, Trump declined to confirm whether she is a Chinese spy, stating he does not know if she was a spy at all and recalling having said so before.
items.title: 'He learnt a big lesson': Trump 'wouldn't mind' Huang's return as Nvidia CEO

items.summary:
Analysts growing concerned a possible pullback in AI financing, especially concerning Nvidia's investments in AI startups and neoclouds - specialized cloud providers renting out AI computing capacity. While the platform expected to continue under interim CEO Colette Kress, there could be an initial pause as company and financiers assess program's future direction. Morningstar analyst Brian Colello noted that Nvidia's CEO transition adds additional uncertainty.

Nvidia's financial partners including Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield Asset Management, Goldman Sachs and KKR still discussing deals to finance AI companies, though one person added there has been no indication from Nvidia of a pause. JPMorgan credit analyst Erica Spear said they do not assume existing commitments change, but new deals could take longer or require more compensation as investors look for reassurance about Nvidia's role.

He promised partnership would bring independent institutional capital into AI infrastructure market while Nvidia limit financial guarantees to maximum 25%.
items.title: Nvidia's AI-Financing Platform Faces Uncertainty After Huang's Departure

items.summary:
A recent episode of Saturday Night Live featured a skit satirizing the controversy surrounding Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, who was mocked for joking that women should "hide your wife" when inviting him over. In the sketch, host John Mulaney played a CIA official tasked with gathering America's most prominent tech billionaires — including Elon Musk to Sam Altman — for training on how to tell apart an actual spy from a woman genuinely interested in them.

Mulaney's CIA official opened by referencing the Huang scandal, asking what lesson the group should take away.
items.title: SNL Jensen Huang skit: 'Hide Your Wife' gang mocked

items.summary:
US President Donald Trump is set to begin an Asia trip on Monday, featuring meetings with regional leaders, trade negotiations, and a first-ever three-way discussion on nuclear weapons involving Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The visit will take him to Manila in the Philippines before he travels to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. The Manila leg is drawing attention over a possible meeting between Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India, as well as discussions around a Quad leaders' summit involving India, the US, Japan and Australia.

The trip comes at a politically difficult time for Trump's administration after his party lost both chambers of Congress in the November midterm elections.

The most significant diplomatic event is expected at the trip's conclusion in Shenzhen, when Trump will hold the first-ever three-way talks with Xi and Putin.
items.title: Trump's Asia Agenda Amid Poll Setback and Nvidia Row

items.summary: On the Kalyan-Kasara railway route, a notorious group known as the 'fataka gang' reportedly struck again by targeting a passenger standing near the door of a moving train. According to police, unidentified members positioned along the tracks allegedly hit Umesh Hari Patil's hand with a stick while he stood in a crowded compartment aboard the Prayagraj-Amrit Bharat Express, travelling from Kalyan toward Bhusawal. The impact caused his iPhone to fall, which the accused then swiftly picked up and escaped with. The stolen handset was reportedly worth around Rs 1. 22 lakh and contained two SIM cards—one each from Jio and BSNL.
items.title: 'Fataka Gang' Snatches ₹1.22 Lakh iPhone From Train Passenger Near Ambivli Station

items.summary: A 38-year-old woman had her iPhone rendered inaccessible after scanning a QR code while attempting to buy an online ticket for the India International Trade Fair (IITF) at Bharat Mandapam, near Gate No. 4 of the fair on Sunday afternoon. According to police, Mohammad Faisal approached her and offered to arrange a discounted ticket for Rs 400 through the official application; when she scanned his QR code, Rs 1,200 was transferred via an online payment app, after which her phone began syncing and became inaccessible. She then received a notification about an unsuccessful login attempt and discovered the money had been deducted from her account.
items.title: Woman's iPhone Locked After Scanning QR Code for IITF Ticket in New Delhi

items.summary:
According to a report by Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple is planning to unveil its first smart glasses next year, with the announcement reportedly set for the Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) in June 2027. The prototypes are internally codenamed "N50" and are described as being thinner than Meta's second-generation smart glasses.

The device will support music playback, phone calls, FaceTime audio, and a front-facing light that indicates when the glasses are charging or in use. Gurman noted that the prototypes can be used while charging, though it remains unclear whether Apple will retain this feature in the final product.
items.title: Apple to Unveil Its First Smart Glasses Next Year: Report

items.summary: Apple is reportedly planning to unveil the second-generation iPhone Air next year, with rumors suggesting camera upgrades, a slimmer design, and improved battery capacity. The device was initially expected to launch alongside the iPhone 18 Pro models in September 2026, but reports now indicate Apple would instead reveal it in March 2027, coinciding with the standard iPhone 18 and entry-level iPhone 18e.
items.title: Rumored iPhone Air 2: Thinner Design, Second Camera, Larger Battery Expected Next Year

items.summary: At the Delhi launch of her memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia Gandhi reflected on the moment she first felt a sense of belonging in India. She recalled that this feeling emerged when people in her husband Rajiv Gandhi's constituency accepted her after his assassination, and she described the 2004 Lok Sabha election victory as a significant milestone marking an important stage in her personal and political journey. Speaking about her relationship with former prime minister Indira Gandhi, Sonia said she was initially awed by and intimidated by her formidable personality but later learned discipline, punctuality, courage and determination from her.
items.title: 'I felt accepted': Sonia Gandhi revisits 2004 Congress win at memoir launch

items.summary:
The Supreme Court ruled on Monday that pollution in the Yamuna has worsened despite substantial spending on cleaning the river, directing civic authorities and the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) to address the problem. A bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Manmohan ordered CPCB to monitor water quality at points where the river enters and exits states, Union territories, and districts—covering 520 drains that discharge wastewater into the Yamuna.

The court emphasized accountability: if water deteriorates on any parameter while passing through a jurisdiction, the concerned administration will be held responsible and penalized. However, the bench acknowledged practical challenges in improving sewage management.
items.title: Supreme Court Raps Admin Over Rising Yamuna Pollution Despite Heavy Spending

items.summary:
The annual UN climate summit in Antalya exposed a widening gap between ambitious climate promises and the money required to implement them, as negotiations entered their final week. Nearly 200 governments faced the recurring question of where funding would come from to turn pledges into action, with adaptation—preparing for already underway climate impacts—identified as the most visible shortage.

The scale of need is stark: a 2026 Adaptation Gap Report by UNEP estimates developing countries will require about $305 billion annually by 2035. Yet international public finance from developed to developing countries reached only $28. 2 billion to $31. 7 billion in 2024, an increase of just $1 billion over the prior year. Even if a commitment made last year to triple international public adaptation finance by 2035 is fully met, it would cover only 20% to 29% of estimated needs.

The wider climate finance dispute remains even more contentious.

The terms of financing matter as well.
items.title: Türkiye Climate Summit's Finance Gap Threatens Its Promise of Action

items.summary: As toxic smog blanketed the National Capital Region and surrounding areas, demand for air purifiers rose sharply. What was once a post-Diwali recurring trend has become part of a broader shift in consumer behaviour. Croma, operated by Tata Group entity, reported that air purifier volumes more than doubled in 2026. Amazon also saw sharp growth, with sales on its platform doubling over the past week and consumers increasingly exploring different models based on room size, filter types and features such as live AQI sensors through AI-based shopping assistance.
items.title: Why Traders Seek GST Cut on Air Purifiers Amid Delhi Smog Crisis
